1.why: All 17 screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate line and letter spacing for body text and labels.

2.why: Instructions are in sentence case with no italics or dense paragraphs; all-caps appears only in the 'NORTHSTAR BANK' brand mark and in the codes themselves, which are data rather than instructions.

3.why: Every screen renders as a single narrow column with full-width fields and buttons that fit a phone-width viewport without horizontal scrolling.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short sentences (e.g., 'We sent a short-lived verification code...'), though terms like 'provisioning value' and 'short-lived' are mild jargon.

5.why: The recovery-code field shows an example placeholder ('ABCD-EFGH-JKLM') and demo credentials are displayed, but the verification-code and authenticator-code fields give no example of expected input format.

6.why: No step requires reading more than two short sentences; the longest text on screen (the otpauth URI and the test-simulation logs) is data, not prose the user must read to proceed.

7.why: The manual secret, otpauth URI, and all recovery codes are rendered as selectable text (and repeated in the logs panel) so they can be copied, though no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code image is rendered anywhere despite the instruction to 'scan the provisioning value'; only a plaintext otpauth:// URI is shown, which cannot be scanned from the same phone.

9.why: Standard labeled text and password inputs are used and the password masks to dots on entry, but autofill or password-manager support cannot be confirmed or refuted from the screenshots alone.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the current step and one large dark-green primary button, but there is no step X-of-Y progress indicator to show position in the flow.

11.why: Each step centres on a single main action, though step 4 shows two green buttons at once ('Create authenticator secret' and 'Enable MFA') and the recovery screen adds a secondary 'Generate replacement recovery codes' button.

12.why: Successful actions produce clear outcome headings such as 'MFA is enabled' with next-step guidance, but failures yield only vague ('Unable to continue sign-in') or raw technical messages with no indication of what comes next.

13.why: Sign-in was retried repeatedly across steps 10–17 without lockout and replacement recovery codes can be generated on demand, though no reveal/hide toggles or verification-code resend link are visible.

14.why: Errors do not blame the user but fail to state the problem or its fix: 'Unable to continue sign-in' is unexplained and step 7 surfaces a raw 'Failed to execute insertBefore on Node' exception.

15.why: The verification code is described as 'short-lived' and the authenticator screen states 'Codes rotate every 30 seconds', so code entry is explicitly time-limited rather than generous.
